# Narration corpus (#904)

Every phrase below is text a renderer produced in this run; none is typed in. Wording is as it is at the commit that ran the export, after the #904 wording audit.

## How it was collected

- **Unit tests.** 628 unit tests ran in the same binary; 331 of them rendered at least one phrase. Each phrase is credited to the test (`tests`) that rendered it.
- **Sweep.** 10 journals were folded one event at a time, and every prefix was drawn at 240x67, 160x45 and 120x33 at the event's own time and 40 s later, and at the planned end and 90 s past it when a trial runs that nothing holds. A started idle (R6) trial freezes its frame, so those are drawn at the first two clocks only, and the sweep asserts the frame reports itself held. 18 scenario cuts were drawn at the three sizes too, with the journal states, help and the journal view (405742 frames in all). Credited as `sweep`.
- **Clauses and templates.** A rendered phrase is cut into clauses at ` · `, ` ─ `, ` │ `, ` → ` and runs of two spaces, and a clause with no letter is dropped. A clause becomes a template by folding its digits, lists and ranges of numbers to `#`, the signs before offsets, hexadecimal ids, gauge and rule glyphs and runs of spaces. The numbers, core lists and error strings a phrase can carry are unbounded, so only the finite templates, forms and branches are claimed as covered.
- **Cuts.** A template that is only a cut of a longer one of the same producer, a truncation ending in `...`, a wrapped row or a column cut, is folded into the longer one; its forms, cases and texts stay on it. A truncation no other template holds whole stays and is marked.
- **Alternatives.** Templates of one producer that differ in one run of up to 3 tokens and agree on every token around it are one line, `before {a | b} after`. Each alternative was rendered in exactly that context, and two positions never vary at once.
- **Provenance.** Each line names its forms, the two least case names that rendered it, and how many renderings there were. A manifest literal is `file:line`.

2996 templates from 46 producers, reduced from 4770 shapes and 122558 distinct texts: 1071 cuts folded in, 1127 templates merged into alternatives, 194 truncations with no full form.

## Regenerating

Both exporters are ignored tests. `<repo>` is the checkout and `<status-export>` an absolute path for the status corpus the second one reads; the first writes it, the second writes this document.

```sh
TOGI_NARRATION_CORPUS=<status-export> \
    cargo test --locked -p togi narration_corpus -- --ignored --nocapture
TOGI_NARRATION_STATUS=<status-export> TOGI_NARRATION_CORPUS=<repo>/docs/narration-phrases.md \
    cargo test --locked -p togi-watch narration_corpus -- --ignored --nocapture
```

## `togi status` corpus

## `togi status`

### Scope and generation

Generated by `TOGI_NARRATION_CORPUS=<absolute file> cargo test --locked -p togi narration_corpus -- --ignored --nocapture` (`crates/togi/src/status/corpus.rs`). Every text below is the status renderer's own output at its only width, 80 columns (`table.rs` `WIDTH`); the status reads no clock, so each journal prefix has exactly one rendering.

- Sweep: every prefix of every `Base::ALL` journal, folded event by event:
  - `base:session`: 9183 events, 9183 prefixes rendered; 45 of them checked equal to `status::render`.
  - `base:concluded`: 10518 events, 10518 prefixes rendered; 44 of them checked equal to `status::render`.
  - `base:unconfirmed`: 11923 events, 11923 prefixes rendered; 49 of them checked equal to `status::render`.
  - `base:later-hunt`: 12520 events, 12520 prefixes rendered; 52 of them checked equal to `status::render`.
  - `base:first-result`: 7179 events, 7179 prefixes rendered; 29 of them checked equal to `status::render`.
  - `base:probe`: 3441 events, 3441 prefixes rendered; 17 of them checked equal to `status::render`.
  - `base:combination`: 5955 events, 5955 prefixes rendered; 24 of them checked equal to `status::render`.
  - `base:crashed-cycle`: 10015 events, 10015 prefixes rendered; 41 of them checked equal to `status::render`.
  - `base:dead-end`: 4194 events, 4194 prefixes rendered; 18 of them checked equal to `status::render`.
- Scenario cuts: the 18 `Scenario::ALL` journals through `status::render`.
- Edge fixtures: 36 recipes from `crates/togi/tests/read/status.rs` and the finite variants no simulated journal reaches (every dead-end condition, defect directions and resets, carried-session forms, telemetry-less R7, Tctl-less evidence, a carried failure with no signal, solo limits three counts deep, a skipped hunt group). Each is rendered through `status::render`; the roster states which ones the status rendered and which it refused, and a refused one contributes no phrase.
- Synthetic renderer cases: 6 cases that hand the private `Status::write` an altered projection or snapshot. They are NOT session states; they show a template branch whose rendering is otherwise unreachable, and the manifest names each such branch as synthetic only.
- Diagnostics: 11 runs of the `status` command itself over state directories on disk; their stderr is listed separately and is not part of the phrase catalogue.
- Renderings recorded: 74987; distinct block templates: 272.

**What is enumerated and what is not.** The unit is a template branch of the status writer, with the values the journals above produce. Unbounded parameters are represented, not enumerated: core IDs and lists, offsets, seqs, counts, durations, timestamps, session IDs, BIOS context strings and defect titles. Recorded journal messages are forwarded verbatim (`in flight`, `carried`, `last decision`, `between-trial evidence`) and so are external error strings in diagnostics; the corpus shows the messages these journals record, not every message `togi-journal`'s `payload/message.rs` can build. The catalogue keeps one actual rendering per template: a block's text with every number as `N` and every run of bare numbers as `N…`. Its cases list the first three fixtures (hand-built ones first) with the number of base-journal prefixes that produced the text and the first and last seq, then the number of further fixtures and renderings. A case ID is `status·<fixture>·80col`.

**Journals the status refused to render** (listed under diagnostics' terms, not phrases):

- `a failed trial carries no signal`: `status·edge:hunt-carried-trial-no-signal·80col`

### Source-branch manifest

Each branch of `crates/togi/src/status.rs` (and the shared words it calls), decided from the executed renderings. A silent branch, one that writes nothing, is proven only by the one fixture named for it. `Reached` says what kind of case rendered the branch: `journal` (a real journal, simulated or rewritten), `synthetic only` (only a case that alters the writer's input), or `unreachable` (no journal the command accepts reaches it, shown by source reading below).

#### Coverage gaps

Every listed branch rendered in at least one case, or is shown unreachable below.

#### Unreachable through the command

- `phase.none` (status.rs:header, phase_clause None): no phase plan: no clause — rendered only by the synthetic case(s) `status·synthetic:no-phase-plan·80col`. `phase_plan()` is `None` only when the tuner state is poisoned or has no run (`togi-tuner/src/phase_plan.rs:159-165`). The run exists from `session.start` (`state.rs:290`), which `render` requires before it writes anything (its `journal.session.is_none()` check), and a poisoned tuner fails `togi_tuner::replay`, which `render` turns into an error before any section (its `Problem::Replay` returns). So a rendered session always has a phase plan and the header's `?` never returns `None`.
- `bios.silent` (status.rs:bios_note, `None => return`): no BIOS note: none confirmed outside phase 1 — rendered only by the synthetic case(s) `status·synthetic:no-confirmed-bios-profile-in-phase-2·80col`; `status·synthetic:no-phase-plan·80col`. The silent branch needs a phase 2 or concluded phase plan with no confirmed BIOS profile. Phase 1 ends only at `Phases::passed_full_cycle` (`phases.rs:203-220`), which errors without a checking profile, and `Later::full_cycle` confirms that same checking profile in the same fold, right after, with `settled` true (`checking/mod.rs:385-393`, `later/mod.rs:171-181, 474-480`). Both are cleared together when a core re-enters search (`cores.rs:180-184`, `later/mod.rs:66-68`, `phases.rs:58-60`). So outside phase 1 a confirmed profile always exists.
- `candidates.solo-none` (status.rs:phase2, candidate solo_limit): SOLO - — rendered only by the synthetic case(s) `status·synthetic:candidate-without-solo-limit·80col`. A candidate row exists only for a core with a gap or a carried move (`phase_plan.rs:134-138`). A gap counts a move of `phase2_moves`, which needs a solo limit and an offset shallower than it (`phases.rs:276-281`); a carried core is one an open round has already moved (`phase_plan.rs:63-74`) or whose offset is deeper than the last passed profile (`phases.rs:269-275`), and only a core with a solo limit moves deeper in phase 2. A solo limit is cleared only when a core re-enters search (`cores.rs:166-168`), which also resets every round (`cores.rs:180-184`). By source reading, every candidate row therefore has a solo limit.

Not mapped branch by branch here: the message builders of `togi-journal/src/payload/message.rs` whose text the status forwards; their renderings appear in the catalogue only as the journals record them.
